title: Chapter 12 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of high availability, load balancing, auto scaling, and HA architecture patterns.

questions.question: What does 'high availability' mean in cloud architecture?
options: The system can survive component failures and remain accessible
The system has no single point of failure
questions.explanation: HA means designing for resilience, accepting that failures happen, and ensuring the system continues to operate.

questions.question: What does RTO stand for?
questions.explanation: RTO is the maximum acceptable time to restore service after a failure.

questions.question: Which of the following is a single point of failure in a VPC?
options: Two Internet Gateways attached to the same VPC
A single NAT Gateway for all private subnets
Multiple route tables for public subnets
Security groups with the same rules
questions.explanation: A single NAT Gateway is an SPOF; if its AZ fails, private instances lose internet access.

questions.question: Which load balancer type operates at Layer 7 and can route based on URL path?
questions.explanation: ALB operates at the application layer (HTTP/HTTPS) and supports content‑based routing.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an ELB health check?
options: To monitor the load balancer's own CPU
To determine which targets are healthy and can receive traffic
To check the health of the client making requests
questions.explanation: Health checks ensure traffic is only sent to healthy targets, enabling automatic failover.

questions.question: Which load balancer provides a static IP per AZ and handles millions of requests per second?
questions.explanation: NLB is designed for extreme performance and low latency, providing static IP addresses in each AZ.

questions.question: What happens when an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group fails its health check?
options: The ASG sends an email notification
The ASG automatically terminates and replaces it
questions.explanation: ASG automatically replaces unhealthy instances to maintain the desired capacity.

questions.question: Which ASG scaling policy keeps a specified metric at a target value, without defining step thresholds?
questions.explanation: Target tracking automatically adjusts capacity to keep a metric near a target value.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a cooldown period in Auto Scaling?
options: To prevent instances from launching too quickly
To wait before evaluating metrics after a scaling action, preventing rapid oscillations
questions.explanation: Cooldown prevents thrashing by giving the system time to stabilise after each scaling action.

questions.question: Which scaling policy type uses machine learning to forecast demand?
questions.explanation: Predictive Scaling analyses historical data and proactively scales ahead of anticipated demand.

questions.question: An ASG can only use EC2 health checks, not ELB health checks.
questions.explanation: False. ASG can incorporate both EC2 status checks and ELB health checks for a more comprehensive health assessment.

questions.question: What is an ASG lifecycle hook used for?
options: To pause instances during launch or termination for custom actions
questions.explanation: Lifecycle hooks let you run scripts or notify services before an instance enters or leaves service.

questions.question: Which Route 53 routing policy sends traffic to a secondary endpoint if the primary fails health checks?
questions.explanation: Failover routing uses a primary/secondary pair and health checks to determine which endpoint to return.

questions.question: RDS Multi‑AZ provides high availability by:
options: Creating read replicas in multiple regions
Synchronously replicating to a standby instance in a different AZ
Backing up to S3 every 5 minutes
questions.explanation: Multi‑AZ maintains a synchronous standby. Read Replicas handle read scaling; they are separate from Multi‑AZ.

questions.question: Aurora storage automatically replicates data across how many AZs?
questions.explanation: Aurora maintains 6 copies of your data across 3 Availability Zones for high durability and availability.

questions.question: Which AWS service is a global CDN that can cache content and provide origin failover?
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches content at edge locations and supports origin groups with automatic failover.

questions.question: AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) is used for:
questions.explanation: FIS helps you test resilience by injecting faults (e.g., terminating instances, throttling network) in a controlled manner.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of using Infrastructure as Code for HA architectures?
options: It enables consistent, repeatable deployments and easier disaster recovery
It eliminates the need for security groups
It replaces the need for monitoring
questions.explanation: IaC allows you to version control your architecture, deploy identical environments, and quickly recreate everything in another region.

questions.question: In an ASG, what does 'scale‑in protection' do?
options: Prevents the ASG from scaling out
Protects specific instances from being terminated during scale‑in
Prevents the ASG from exceeding max capacity
Protects the launch template from modification
questions.explanation: Scale‑in protection marks instances so the ASG will not terminate them automatically, useful for long‑running tasks.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach for NAT Gateway high availability?
options: Use one NAT Gateway per region
Deploy one NAT Gateway per Availability Zone
Use a single NAT Gateway with enhanced networking
questions.explanation: Deploying one NAT Gateway per AZ ensures that if one AZ fails, private subnets in other AZs retain internet connectivity.

questions.question: Which metric is commonly used with target tracking to maintain a consistent user experience?
options: Average CPU utilization or request count per target
questions.explanation: Average CPU utilization and ALB request count per target are popular target metrics for autoscaling web applications.

questions.question: An ASG can launch instances across multiple Availability Zones automatically.
questions.explanation: True. You specify multiple subnets (each in a different AZ) when creating the ASG, and it distributes instances across them.

questions.question: DynamoDB Global Tables provide:
questions.explanation: Global Tables replicate data across regions and allow reads and writes in any region.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a Launch Template and a Launch Configuration?
options: Launch Templates support versioning and are the modern replacement
Launch Templates only work with Spot instances
questions.explanation: Launch Templates are the newer, more flexible option with versioning and more features. Launch Configurations are legacy.

questions.question: You need to ensure your application survives a full AWS region outage. Which strategy should you employ?
options: Multi‑region deployment with Route 53 failover and data replication
Single‑AZ with very fast EBS snapshots
questions.explanation: Multi‑region is required to survive a regional disaster. Multi‑AZ protects against AZ failure, not a full region outage.
